question: Can the unchanged authored-scene Windows recipient start and expose its actual owner when its original script is invoked directly in the explicitly observed restricted same-user PowerShell context (Administrators deny-only, medium integrity, elevation fields recorded), without changing the package, account, ACL, execution policy or URL reservations?
beneficiary: A prospective recipient whose access prerequisites need evidence distinct from prior administrative-runner success. This specific restricted-token observation does not establish ordinary-user Windows access.

baseline.managed_application: The same unchanged ten managed files, compiled journal identity and actual SceneSession/RequestExpedition owners.
baseline.runtime: The existing private official .NET10.0.12 win-x64 runtime with notices; no regenerated recipient ZIP.
baseline.earlier_limit: Actual Windows Server2025 administrative token; not evidence for this new token context.

hypotheses.prediction: The unchanged package starts and the actual /state endpoint responds when invoked directly in the observed restricted same-user PowerShell context, with the same protected package and without machine changes.
hypotheses.decision: Retain bounded access evidence; a replacement transport is not justified merely by the earlier administrative token.

hypotheses.prediction: The package actually exits nonzero before serving under the selected observed context.
hypotheses.decision: Retain the exact refusal stage and diagnostic. A specific dependency, including HTTP.sys permission, requires pertinent evidence rather than attribution from timing or token alone.

hypotheses.prediction: Token creation, helper launch, identity observation or bounded execution fails or times out before application access can be evaluated.
hypotheses.decision: Classify application access as inconclusive; neither successful access nor confirmed application refusal.

hypotheses.prediction: Results depend on the same account/profile, filesystem permissions, URL reservations or hosted environment rather than general ordinary-user Windows behavior.
hypotheses.decision: Restrict claims to the recorded context; no ordinary-user population, Windows10/11 or physical-device generalization.

context_selection.first: If Windows genuinely provides an existing linked limited token, record that separate branch and its actual resulting properties; do not assume it exists or replace a failed lookup with an ordinary-user claim.
context_selection.fallback: CreateRestrictedToken with DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE, Administrators SID deny-only and medium integrity. This remains a constructed restricted same-user context even if Windows reports elevated=true/elevation_type1, as in the initial run. It is not a fresh standard-user account or a demonstrated non-elevated token.
context_selection.required_observation: Record the parent, actual selected child observer and actual PowerShell process token: administrator membership, Administrators deny-only, medium integrity, elevated flag and elevation type. Require administrator=false, medium integrity and Administrators deny-only for this declared restricted boundary. Retain elevated/elevation_type exactly; do not relabel elevated=true as non-elevated or ordinary-user access. The native dotnet application inherits through the unchanged direct invocation; its own token is not independently queried.
forbidden_interventions: Creating accounts or changing account membership
Elevation or enabling privileges to make the application pass
Changing execution policy or URLACL reservations
Changing machine security settings, protected source, package payload or runtime notices
Relaxing existing integrity/security gates or counting timeout as refusal
context_selection.elevation_fields: Observed data, never normalized to the intended condition. The initial elevated=true value remains preserved and limits the claim.

method: Preserve all earlier protocols/artifacts. Declare revision4 before execution, retain SDK10.0.401 and initial/final source/protocol/recipient hashes. Remove only redundant PowerShell wrapper redirection; use already-owned native standard handles and keep all construction/context failures inconclusive.
Verify the unchanged recipient archive and extracted inventory; retain baseline notices, managed assembly identity and source closure.
Record Windows version/architecture, executed commit and token-selection outcome without dumping credentials or environment secrets.

In the already-selected PowerShell, query that actual process token by PID, then invoke the unchanged run-demo.ps1 directly. Use a fresh external save directory and the original private runtime; do not create a second recipient PowerShell.

Observe the restricted PowerShell context and bounded application attempt, retain actual process exit/stdout/stderr and poll the real owner endpoint. Native dotnet token inheritance is inferred through the unchanged script and explicitly not independently queried.
Classify actual successful access, actual nonzero application refusal, or inconclusive instrument/context/timeout separately. Preserve all observed diagnostics and owned-process cleanup.
Check initial/final instrument and inherited-input identities; a source mutation invalidates the run rather than silently updating the claim.
Compare the observed dependency against coherent product/source alternatives before any transport adaptation; do not automatically rebuild a package or repeat prior matrices.
refusal_rule: Require the unchanged original script actually to be invoked and an observed integer nonzero exit with its retained diagnostic. A second-process creation failure before invocation, timeout, missing exit, helper/token/identity failure or unobserved declared context remains inconclusive. A nonzero script exit alone does not identify an HTTP.sys cause.
success_rule: Require the actual declared restricted PowerShell context, unchanged original-script invocation and a response from the actual package owner endpoint. Preserve observed elevation fields. This supports only that restricted same-user context, never general ordinary-user or non-elevated access.
adaptation_rule: A later transport change is justified only by an observed consequential dependency, with a separate refutable acceptance and actual consumer. Preserve or explicitly resolve compiled journal/save compatibility; do not create a second gameplay owner, fallback grants or fabricated return/delivery.
counting: This baseline is selection evidence for one coherent contribution. Repeated software observations, token branches, compilation and packaging support are not independent participants, studies, candidate attempts or extra workstream units.
maturity: Build/Operations remains incomplete under its retained licensed Unity Editor, activation/modules and production Windows acceptance. No Unity or Steam execution is claimed.
limitations: Revision2 observed original-script refusal before native dotnet execution; it is not evidence that RequestJournal, gameplay or HTTP.sys refused the restricted token. Its exact stdout/stderr and actual token fields remain in the retained artifact.

Initial trial remains inconclusive: elevated=true/elevation_type1 were actually observed, and no application refusal or HTTP.sys cause was established. Revision2 changes the declared operational condition and instrument topology prospectively, not the historical result.
The linked limited and constructed restricted contexts must be named separately; a constructed token is not automatically ordinary-user Windows evidence.
The same account/profile and filesystem environment remain shared; this is not an enforced sandbox or a fresh participant/device.
No Windows10/11 breadth, physical device, human author/player approval, comprehension, enjoyment, commercial clearance or production ownership claim.
No general save migration, power-loss, distributed account or production security guarantee.
A refusal diagnostic can suggest a mechanism but does not establish every causal condition without an appropriate control.
The actual observed token belongs to the PowerShell invoking the original script; the nested native dotnet token is inferred by inheritance and is not independently queried.
scientific_influence: SCI-013/014/076/077: predeclared rival explanations, exact observed token as the operational condition, method selected by the claim, and explicit inconclusive/repeated-observation boundaries.

supersedes.policy: Retain all earlier protocols/actual artifacts. No prior result becomes application or HTTP.sys execution.

revision_reason: Revision3 retained the same native-command encoding refusal before the C#host. The private dotnet.exe identity controls had executed successfully without the additional PowerShell1>/2> redirection layer. Revision4 removes only that unnecessary outer redirection and reads the actual standard-output/error files already owned by the C#launcher. Token, executable, original script, process identity checks and standard handles stay unchanged. No transport adaptation is yet justified.

process_topology.initial: The selected PowerShell launched a separate recipient PowerShell with ProcessStartInfo.Start. That instrument call failed Access is denied before a recipient token/application outcome existed.
process_topology.revision2: The already-selected restricted PowerShell queries its actual own PID token and invokes the unchanged run-demo.ps1 directly with the PowerShell call operator. No second recipient PowerShell is created. The original script directly invokes its private native dotnet process.
process_topology.why_permitted: This changes instrument process topology to avoid an unneeded process-creation dependency; it does not grant permissions, elevate, change an account/policy/URLACL, edit the package or waive a confirmed application refusal.
process_topology.application_token_limit: Actual token observation is of the PowerShell process executing the original script. Nested native application token inheritance is inferred from the unchanged direct invocation, not independently queried.
process_topology.revision3: Create three owned inheritable standard handles (NUL input, create-new output/error files), pass STARTF_USESTDHANDLES with CreateProcessAsUser inheritHandles=true, then keep revision2 direct unchanged-script invocation and actual process-token checks. No account, token privilege elevation, ACL, execution policy, URL reservation or package changes.
process_topology.revision4: Existing restricted PowerShell invokes original run-demo.ps1 with the call operator and no extra PowerShell redirection; native output/error flow through the supported C#owned inherited standard handles to selected-child.stdout/stderr files. Parent classifies actual exit/HTTP and retains exact diagnostics.
